# Results — Study 763 (Puell-Multiple)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — David Puell's
**Puell Multiple** (2019): daily Bitcoin miner *issuance value* divided by its trailing 365-day
average is a contrarian cycle timer — **> 4 = overheated top (sell), < 0.5 = undervalued bottom
(buy)**. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `9529d5277775` (BTC-USD daily close).*

## Data stamp — a reconstruction, not a proxy

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **BTC-USD** close, 4,305 rows, 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-30 (price-only == total-return; BTC pays no yield) |
| Issuance schedule | the **known Bitcoin halving step function** (hardcoded in [`puell_multiple/data.py`](../puell_multiple/data.py)): block reward 25 (pre-2016-07-09) → 12.5 → 6.25 (post-2020-05-11) → **3.125** (post-2024-04-20), at the protocol 144 blocks/day |
| Metric | `Puell(t) = 144·reward(t)·price(t) / trailing-365d mean of the same`; **3,941** daily values 2015-09-16 → 2026-06-30 (min **0.40**, median **1.12**, max **5.95**) |
| Signal rule | contrarian bands — top **Puell ≥ 4** (sell / stand aside), bottom **Puell ≤ 0.5** (buy), else neutral |
| Execution | Puell known at the close of day t; the timer's exposure applies to the return of day **t+1** (one-day lag, the study's single documented convention) |
| Costs | 10 bps one-way × NAV on every flip; long/flat, no borrow |

**Why this is a reconstruction and not a labelled proxy.** The Puell Multiple's only non-price
input is the coinbase issuance, which is a *deterministic, publicly known* step function of the
halving schedule — not an estimated on-chain series. And the constant 144 blocks/day **cancels
in the ratio** (it multiplies both numerator and denominator), so the multiple is invariant to
it. The **one** named approximation is that real daily block counts wobble a few percent around
144 (difficulty retargets every ~2 weeks); that variation largely cancels in the ratio and never
moves a threshold crossing. Consequence worth stating plainly: *within* a halving epoch the Puell
Multiple reduces to `price(t) / trailing-365d-mean(price)` — a 365-day price ratio — and the only
thing it adds on top is a mechanical ~1-year suppression after each halving (the denominator
still holds pre-halving days at double the reward). (The original, most-cited Puell Multiple is
issuance-only; some later variants add transaction fees — a different, non-reconstructable metric.)

**Single-survivor (named on the Signal axis):** BTC is the one crypto that survived and 100×+'d,
and the Puell Multiple is *mechanically derived from BTC's own price*. Every band below is read
off a handful of that one asset's cycles.

## 1 · Predictive regression — does log(Puell) forecast forward returns?

`r_{t→t+h} = a + b·log(Puell_t) + e`, Newey-West (HAC) *t*, lag = h (forward windows overlap).
A contrarian gauge needs **b < 0** with **|t| ≥ 2**.

| horizon | slope b | HAC *t* | R² | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| +30d | +0.0284 | **+0.67** | 0.004 | 3,911 |
| +90d | +0.0027 | **+0.02** | 0.000 | 3,851 |
| +180d | −0.1616 | **−0.74** | 0.016 | 3,761 |

The slope is not even *stably* the contrarian sign — positive at 30/90 days, negative at 180 —
and **no horizon clears |t| ≥ 2** (best |t| = 0.74). R² is ~0 everywhere. Adding BTC's own
trailing-180d price momentum (a horse race at 90 days) leaves the Puell slope at HAC *t* = −1.76
(price-momentum *t* = +1.70) — still short of the bar, and only borderline-negative once the
price trend is partialled out. **log(Puell) carries no robust forward information for BTC returns.**

## 2 · Band forward returns — the "tops & bottoms" claim, dissected

Mean forward BTC return by Puell band vs the unconditional distribution; Welch *t*; random-date
placebo (20 seeds × 1,000 draws of the same day-count; right-tailed for the buy band, left-tailed
for the sell band — the direction the contrarian claim predicts).

| horizon | band | mean fwd | median | hit | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| +90d | **bottom** (Puell ≤ 0.5) | **+2.0%** | −1.8% | 0.44 | −11.10 | **1.000** |
| +90d | neutral | +24.0% | +11.2% | 0.61 | +0.65 | — |
| +90d | **top** (Puell ≥ 4) | **−44.2%** | −46.8% | 0.00 | −19.14 | **0.000** |
| +30d | bottom | +6.8% | +6.5% | 0.75 | +0.08 | 0.479 |
| +30d | top | −17.1% | −20.3% | 0.14 | −4.60 | 0.000 |
| +180d | bottom | +60.9% | +49.6% | 0.61 | +0.67 | 0.304 |
| +180d | top | −56.9% | −59.9% | 0.00 | −43.47 | 0.000 |

Two things break the folklore here:

- **The "buy the bottom" half is empty.** After a Puell ≤ 0.5 reading, BTC's 90-day forward
  return averages **+2.0%** — *worse* than a neutral day's **+24.0%** (placebo *p* = 1.000: a
  random day does at least as well essentially always). At 30 and 180 days the bottom band is
  statistically indistinguishable from a coin-flip day (placebo *p* = 0.48, 0.30). Buying deep
  Puell lows did **not** beat just being in the market.
- **The "sell the top" half is one blow-off, dressed as statistics.** The Puell ≥ 4 band's
  forward returns are hugely negative and its placebo *p* rounds to 0.000 — but the band spans
  just **22 days**, and those 22 days are **a single episode**: three contiguous runs all inside
  2017-12-04 → 2018-01-06 — the 2017 blow-off top and its immediate echo. The Welch *t* of −19
  (90d) / −43 (180d) treats 22 autocorrelated days from one event as 22 independent draws — it is
  **fake precision**, not evidence. n_effective ≈ 1.

So on the real tape the Puell bands mark exactly **one** top (2017) and **zero** tradable
bottoms.

## 3 · Buy-low / sell-high timer vs buy-and-hold

Long BTC, step to cash whenever Puell ≥ 4 (one-day lag), 10 bps one-way × NAV per flip;
price-only; same [first Puell day → tape end] window for both legs.

| strategy | total return | CAGR | Sharpe | exposure |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Puell buy-low/sell-high timer | +24,841% | +66.80%/yr | +1.114 | 99.4% of the time |
| Buy-and-hold BTC | **+25,461%** | **+67.18%/yr** | +1.107 | 100% of the time |
| **Timer − buy-and-hold** | — | **−0.97%/yr** | — (HAC *t* = **−0.21**) | 7 flips |

The timer is **99.4% buy-and-hold**: Puell only clears 4 at the very peak of a blow-off, so the
cash window is a few weeks, and by the time the multiple has cooled below 4 the bulk of the
ensuing bear (e.g. most of 2018) is still ahead — the rule re-enters straight into it. It
**trails** buy-and-hold net of costs, and the −0.97%/yr shortfall is insignificant (HAC
*t* = −0.21). Sweeping the sell threshold only confirms a knob-tuning artefact — the timer trails
buy-and-hold at **every** setting:

| sell threshold | total return | exposure | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Puell ≥ 3.0 | +18,921% | 97.6% | 1.09 |
| Puell ≥ 3.5 | +20,377% | 98.9% | 1.09 |
| Puell ≥ 4.0 | +24,841% | 99.4% | 1.11 |
| Puell ≥ 4.5 | +22,944% | 99.6% | 1.10 |
| *buy-and-hold* | *+25,461%* | *100%* | *1.11* |

Any CAGR the timer shows is just long exposure to a 100×+ survivor, minus a little.

## 4 · Synthetic positive control — the machinery is honest

The same predictive regression is pointed at a deterministic synthetic (Puell, price) world with
a **tunable** contrarian link; no network.

| world | slope | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| planted contrarian β = 0.50 (seed 763) | −11.78 | **−26.09** |
| null β = 0.00, **20 seeds** | ~0 | mean **+0.06** (sd 1.22), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20** |

The detector recovers a genuine planted contrarian link cleanly and reads ~zero on the null. The
engine can find the effect when it's there; the real BTC tape simply has no such link. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** log(Puell) does not forecast forward BTC returns (best HAC *t* = 0.74, sign
  not even stably contrarian; horse-race *t* = −1.76, still short of 2; R² ≈ 0). The "buy the
  bottom" band underperforms a neutral day (+2.0% vs +24.0% at 90d, placebo *p* = 1.000). The one
  striking number — the top band's −44%/90d — is a **single** 2017-18 blow-off top (22 clustered
  days, n_effective ≈ 1) whose Welch *t* = −19 is autocorrelation fake-precision. No robust
  *t* ≥ 2 anywhere on the real tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The buy-low/sell-high timer is 99.4% buy-and-hold and **trails** it
  net of costs at every sell threshold (best +24,841% vs +25,461%; −0.97%/yr, HAC *t* = −0.21).
  Puell clears 4 only at the top itself, and the rule re-enters before the bear is done. Any CAGR
  is long exposure to a single survivor.
- **"Times tops & bottoms?" — BUSTED.** The bottom-call is empty (worse than a random day) and
  the top-call is one historical episode that does not survive as a trade.
